title: CEO Interview with Timothy Regan of IN2FAB - Semiwiki
gist: IN2FAB founder Timothy Regan describes his company's business of migrating silicon-proven analog and mixed-signal IP between process nodes and foundries using proprietary EDA software plus engineering services, and outlines plans to extend migration to full SoCs and to build narrow, EDA-specific AI rather than adopt general-purpose LLMs.

insights.claim: Timothy Regan built his career in analog/mixed-signal design and its supporting EDA technologies, beginning in linear engineering at Texas Instruments, then working as an applications specialist at GE-Calma and Valid Logic Systems, followed by 10 years as managing director at Design Resources Ltd providing physical semiconductor design services and EDA consulting.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Establishes deep, multi-decade analog/EDA domain expertise behind IN2FAB's technology claims, relevant for assessing founder credibility in a services/IP-migration niche.
insights.quote: His career began in linear engineering at Texas Instruments.

insights.claim: Timothy Regan founded IN2FAB in 2000 and serves as the company's president and CTO.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A 25+ year-old founder-led company suggests a mature, established player in the semiconductor IP-migration services niche rather than a new entrant.
insights.quote: He founded IN2FAB in 2000 and serves as the company’s president and CTO.

themes.theme: Core business: IP migration between process nodes and foundries

insights.claim: IN2FAB is a semiconductor software and engineering company specializing in migrating and retargeting semiconductor designs between process technologies and foundries, combining proprietary EDA software with decades of hands-on engineering experience to help customers reuse silicon-proven IP instead of redesigning it from scratch.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defines a specific, addressable niche in the EDA/semiconductor services market -- IP reuse across foundries -- that reduces redesign cost and risk for chip customers.
insights.quote: IN2FAB is a semiconductor software and engineering company specializing in the migration and retargeting of semiconductor designs between process technologies and foundries.

insights.claim: IN2FAB's experience spans virtually every major foundry and many leading IDMs, with customers ranging from specialist IP companies to some of the world's largest semiconductor businesses.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Broad foundry/IDM coverage suggests IN2FAB's migration technology is not locked to a single ecosystem, widening its addressable customer base.
insights.quote: Our experience spans virtually every major foundry and many leading IDMs, with customers ranging from specialist IP companies to some of the world’s largest semiconductor businesses.

insights.claim: IN2FAB's engineering teams have taken hundreds of circuits through design and tapeout over the years, giving practical experience in what is required to migrate circuits to a manufacturable, working product.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A track record of hundreds of successful tapeouts is a concrete proof point of execution capability that differentiates a services vendor from a pure software tool provider.
insights.quote: Over the years, our engineering teams have helped customers around the world take hundreds of circuits through design and tapeout.
insights.locator: Our experience is backed by a long history

themes.theme: Application depth in analog and mixed-signal

insights.claim: IN2FAB's deepest expertise is in analog and mixed-signal design, particularly complex custom layouts, with work spanning data converters, PLLs, power management, RF, sensors, memory, and other precision and high-performance circuits, plus custom digital and specialized circuits.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific circuit categories -- data converters, PLLs, power management, RF -- where IN2FAB's migration technology has proven applicability, useful for scoping which chip companies are its natural customers.
insights.quote: Over the years, we have worked on a broad range of applications including data converters, PLLs, power management, RF, sensors, memory, and other precision and high-performance circuits.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: Migration is rarely a one-size-fits-all process; the approach must reflect the characteristics of both the source and target process technologies, given differences in device architectures, design rules, PDKs, database technologies, and physical design methodologies across mature and advanced nodes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A reusable mental model for evaluating any IP-migration vendor: breadth of process/foundry experience matters because migration complexity varies by source and target technology.
insights.quote: That breadth is important because migration is rarely a simple matter of applying the same process to every design—the approach must reflect the characteristics of both the source and target technologies.
insights.locator: One of our strengths is the breadth

insights.claim: Shrinking product windows mean chip companies can no longer afford to spend six to twelve months recreating layouts for a new process technology while also wanting to protect years of prior engineering investment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Quantifies the time cost (6-12 months) of manual redesign that IP-migration technology aims to eliminate, a concrete efficiency metric for evaluating the value proposition.
insights.quote: Product windows continue to shrink, and companies can’t afford to spend six to twelve months recreating layouts for a new technology.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: A shortage of experienced analog and custom IC engineers is a major industry challenge, and companies would rather deploy these scarce engineers on new products than on recreating designs already proven in silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Points to a structural talent bottleneck in analog design that creates durable demand for migration automation and outsourced engineering services.
insights.quote: Another major challenge is the shortage of experienced analog and custom engineers.

insights.claim: As process technologies become more complex, manual redesign increases the risk of subtle implementation errors and extends verification cycles, making predictable migration increasingly difficult.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Links rising process complexity directly to higher redesign risk, reinforcing the case for automated migration tools over manual redesign as nodes advance.
insights.quote: As process technologies become more complex, manual redesign also increases the risk of subtle implementation errors and extends verification cycles, making predictable migration increasingly difficult.

insights.claim: Many semiconductor companies historically respond to the need to move IP to a new process by redesigning the circuit or avoiding retargeting altogether, leaving valuable silicon-proven IP stranded on older process nodes because migration is perceived as expensive, risky, and disruptive.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies an industry-wide default behavior (abandoning IP on old nodes) that IN2FAB positions itself against, framing a market opportunity for migration-as-a-service.
insights.quote: Many organizations leave valuable silicon-proven IP on older process nodes because migration is perceived as expensive, risky, and disruptive.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: IN2FAB's migration technology is designed to complement customers' existing EDA tools and workflows rather than requiring them to purchase and deploy new EDA tool suites, minimizing disruption and deployment costs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A low-friction integration strategy (working within existing toolchains) lowers the adoption barrier versus competitors requiring new EDA platform purchases.
insights.quote: Instead of requiring companies to purchase and deploy expensive new EDA tool suites, our solutions integrate into existing design, verification, and signoff flows, minimizing disruption and reducing deployment costs.

themes.theme: Roadmap: SoC-scale migration and narrow AI

insights.claim: IN2FAB is extending its migration technology beyond complex analog and custom layout into digital standard-cell designs, hierarchical blocks, memories, and ultimately complete SoCs, developing tools to analyze and manipulate large hierarchical designs while preserving connectivity, placement, and routing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals a roadmap expansion from a niche analog service into full-chip (SoC) migration, which would substantially broaden IN2FAB's addressable market if achieved.
insights.quote: The goal is to make migration practical at the SoC level rather than treating each block as an isolated engineering project.
insights.locator: What new features or technology are you working on?

insights.claim: IN2FAB is combining emerging AI technology with its existing codebase to build focused AI that operates directly within semiconductor design environments and understands EDA-specific languages such as Cadence SKILL, rather than pairing a general-purpose LLM with EDA manuals.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A domain-specific AI approach, contrarian to the general-purpose LLM trend, claims to deliver capable EDA AI with a much smaller compute/power/cost footprint -- relevant to evaluating AI strategy differentiation among EDA vendors.
insights.quote: Rather than simply combining a general-purpose LLM with EDA manuals, we’re developing focused AI around the actual software and engineering context, including languages such as Cadence SKILL and other EDA-specific technologies.
insights.locator: We’re also combining emerging AI technology

insights.claim: IN2FAB believes its narrow, EDA-context-specific AI approach can deliver highly capable AI for EDA with a dramatically smaller computational, power, and cost footprint than general-purpose AI systems, while keeping proprietary customer data within the customer's own environment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Frames a cost/efficiency and data-privacy argument for specialized small AI models over general-purpose LLMs in EDA workflows, a thesis relevant to the broader debate on domain-specific versus foundation-model AI in engineering software.
insights.quote: We believe this approach can deliver highly capable AI for EDA with a dramatically smaller computational, power, and cost footprint than general-purpose AI systems, while keeping proprietary data within the customer’s environment.
insights.locator: We’re also combining emerging AI technology

insights.claim: IN2FAB customer engagements start with a technical and strategic discussion of a specific migration challenge, followed by an assessment of technical complexity and detailed schedule and pricing showing how much of the existing design can be preserved versus requiring engineering intervention.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Describes a structured sales/engagement process that gives prospective customers a clear cost-benefit picture before committing, relevant to understanding sales cycle and deal structure in this services niche.
insights.quote: From there, we assess the technical complexity of the project and provide detailed schedule and pricing.

insights.claim: IN2FAB offers a flexible commercial model: customers with in-house engineering resources can purchase licenses of the migration software and self-perform projects, others use IN2FAB's engineering team as a design service, and a hybrid combining both is also available.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A dual software-license-plus-services revenue model diversifies IN2FAB's monetization and customer fit versus a pure-software or pure-services competitor.
insights.quote: Those with in-house engineering resources can purchase licenses of our migration software and perform projects themselves, while others use our engineering team as a design service.
insights.locator: Customers can then choose the model
